title: Payment Protection Claim Filing and Documentation Standards
content:
Every Payment Protection claim runs on four clocks: filing after the loss, documents after filing, the decision after documents, and proof while benefits continue. Each is set per plan.

## Claim clocks by plan

| Plan | Claim filed within (calendar days after the loss date) | Required documents received within (calendar days after filing), or the claim is denied | Claim decided within (business days after all documents are received) | Proof of continued disability or unemployment while benefits are paid (every so many calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Protection Life | 90 | 30 | 10 | 30 |
| Payment Protection Life and Disability | 90 | 30 | 10 | 30 |
| Payment Protection Complete | 90 | 30 | 10 | 30 |
| Joint Payment Protection Life | 90 | 30 | 10 | 30 |
| Joint Payment Protection Life and Disability | 90 | 30 | 10 | 30 |
| Joint Payment Protection Complete | 90 | 30 | 10 | 30 |

## Documents required by claim type

The same list applies in all six plans.

| Claim type | Documents required |
|---|---|
| Death | death certificate |
| Disability | physician statement |
| Involuntary unemployment | unemployment benefit letter and employer separation notice |

## Standard notes

- The filing clock and the document clock run in calendar days; the decision clock runs in business days.
- An involuntary unemployment claim needs both documents listed; one of the two alone does not complete it.
- The decision clock starts only once all required documents have been received.
